title: Mortara wins the finale but Wittmann takes the title
dek: Edoardo Mortara won Race 2 at Hockenheim for Audi by 3.040 seconds from Christian Vietoris, but Marco Wittmann's fourth place gave him the DTM title by four points.

chapters.title: A 17-point gap and one race
text: Saturday had narrowed the title fight without settling it. Miguel Molina won Race 1 for Audi and Marco Wittmann finished second, but Edoardo Mortara climbed from eighth on the grid to third, leaving him 17 points behind with 25 for a win still to come. Wittmann led the standings on 194 points to Mortara's 177 and needed to finish fifth or better on Sunday to be sure of the championship; Jamie Green had been eliminated on 141. Mortara needed at least second place, and even a win would only be enough if Wittmann finished seventh or lower. Only the 25 points of Sunday's race were left to win.

chapters.title: Da Costa on pole again, the title rivals on row three
text: António Félix da Costa took his second pole position of the weekend in his final DTM qualifying session, going to the top of the order in the closing minutes with a 1:32.632 and improving to 1:32.525. Gary Paffett's Mercedes was 0.014 seconds behind, with Tom Blomqvist third in the RBM BMW, 0.064 off the pole time, followed by Maxime Martin. Timo Glock had set the first benchmark for BMW, which Paffett and Green beat in turn, and Wittmann had climbed to second on his early runs before the final-run shuffle pushed him back.

The title rivals were on the third row. Wittmann was fifth with a 1:32.616 and Mortara sixth, just 0.028 seconds slower, after a session disrupted by a technical problem with his Audi that left him short of running. Wickens was seventh, Glock eighth, Christian Vietoris ninth and Green tenth, so that five BMWs started in the top ten. Di Resta qualified only 18th, while Molina, Saturday's winner, was 22nd on the grid, with Rast 23rd and Maximilian Götz at the back of the field in 24th.

chapters.title: Mortara sweeps to the front
text: Mortara lost places at the start from sixth on the grid, but he recovered quickly. He passed Wickens, Martin and Blomqvist in the first two laps while da Costa led from Paffett. Their fight ended when Paffett tagged the back of the BMW as it moved across to take the racing line, sending da Costa off the track. Paffett was given a drive-through penalty and da Costa, who said afterwards that Paffett had been impatient, went on to retire from the race.

That promoted Wittmann to the lead, for only a short time. Mortara was past him by lap six, and the race turned into a matter of how far Wittmann could fall. Mortara built a lead of more than six seconds before the stops.

chapters.title: Mercedes drivers pass Wittmann
text: The mandatory stops put the championship under pressure. Mortara and Wittmann both stopped late, and Wittmann rejoined behind the Mercedes of Vietoris and di Resta and, for a time, Blomqvist's BMW. Fifth place was enough for the title, but he was no longer comfortable. Di Resta, who had climbed from 18th on the grid, did not give way when Wittmann tried to go through, and once the Audis that had yet to stop were out of the way, Vietoris and di Resta settled in second and third.

Wittmann passed Blomqvist and then settled into fourth, with fellow BMW drivers Glock, Martin and Blomqvist following in his wake. Glock set the fastest lap of the race on lap 30. Behind them, several cars did not see the flag: Adrien Tambay, Farfus, Rosenqvist and Daniel Juncadella were all out.

chapters.title: Mortara wins, Wittmann champion by four points
text: Mortara crossed the line in 1:02:52.131, 3.040 seconds ahead of Vietoris, for Audi's win in the final race of the year. Di Resta completed the podium in third, 4.294 seconds behind, a recovery from 18th on the grid that gave Mercedes two podium places. Wittmann took the flag in fourth, 5.030 seconds back, and won the title with 206 points to Mortara's 202.

Glock, Martin and Blomqvist took the next three places, Green was eighth, Wickens ninth and Martin Tomczyk took the last point in tenth on the final start of his DTM career. Paffett finished 15th and da Costa was out after 21 laps. Molina, who had won on Saturday, was 14th. Audi's Nico Müller and Rockenfeller were 13th and 11th.

chapters.title: Wittmann's second title, Audi's bitter win
text: Wittmann said he had tried to bring the car home, called it unbelievable to be champion for the second time and said that his 2014 title had come with a more dominant car and more wins, while this year the team had had to be clever. It was his second DTM crown, following the 2014 one, and BMW's Jens Marquardt said his consistency and speed had made the difference in a close field.

For Audi it was a bitter victory. Mortara won the race, and Audi took the manufacturers' title and the team title for Audi Sport Team Abt Sportsline, but he fell four points short of Wittmann. Audi's DTM chief Dieter Gass called it the bitterest win he could remember and said that far fewer than ten points had been missing, the number the marque felt it had lost at Zandvoort in July. Mortara said that it was very disappointing but that there was nothing he could do about it.

Mercedes finished third in the manufacturers' standings, but Ulrich Fritz said the double podium was what the team had wanted at the end of the season and that it would try to come back stronger in 2017. Several drivers also left the series. Da Costa will not return, and said afterwards that he would have liked a podium in his last race, while Tomczyk and Timo Scheider also completed their final DTM weekends.

Wittmann finished the season on 206 points, four ahead of Mortara on 202, with Green third on 145, Wickens fourth on 124, di Resta fifth on 116 and Blomqvist sixth on 113. Blomqvist called sixth in the standings a good result, saying the key had been the team's qualifying form. With that, the nine race weekends of 2016, 18 races in all, were over.

facts.v: Marco Wittmann finished fourth and won the 2016 title with 206 points to Edoardo Mortara's 202.
